title: ThreadHelper: the serendipity plugin Twitter killed
summary:
Two builders (@nosilverv and @exgenesis) shipped a browser extension that literally sits beside your tweet composer and whispers “hey, didn’t you already say something smart about this?”—then Twitter’s API changes quietly put it in the ground.

Arc is clean: **[trigger]** people like @easoncxz cataloging how badly Twitter needs power-tools (search your own likes, thread UIs, timeline replay) → **[peak]** Oct 2020 launch hype where @exgenesis sells ThreadHelper as more than search (“redirects the flow of attention to *IRRIGATE THE PAST*,” “like Roam, but multiplayer-first,” eventual p2p/user-sovereign data) and @nosilverv drops the “visa-as-a-service” origin story (thread like @visakanv/@0x49fa98 without doing the manual work), plus the big thank-you rollcall (Emergent Ventures grant via @tylercowen, UI help from @henrywfisher, early push from @garybasin, 50 alpha testers). The funniest user truth serum: @mechanical_monk saying the idle mode is “the fucking pond in the narcissus story” because it makes you sit there refreshing your own past bangers. Others echo the dependency: @TylerAlterman claims it “deepened my relationship with my exobrain” and mobile Twitter now feels “onerous”; @RobertHaisfield loves that it surfaces tweets he wouldn’t have thought to search for; @RichDecibels starts requesting toggles like “Fuck Up Your Serendipity Generator” when username-matching breaks results.

**[outcome/current state]** there’s a brief second-act builder high in 2021 (“new ThreadHelper is so good, you guys are gonna fucking die”), then 2022 open-sourcing (“gif to the community”), and by late 2023 @nosilverv confirms the obvious post-Elon reality: “did the api changes break it?” “yes ☹️.” The residue is the vocabulary: *“irrigate the past,” “serendipity generator,” “visakanv-as-a-service,” “exobrain”*—and the enduring itch it scratched: Twitter made you produce a mountain of thoughts, then gave you no humane way to reuse them.
